chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his father (peace be upon them both).
Regarding the saying of God, Blessed and Exalted: "And they ask you: Is it true? Say: Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true" [10:53].
He said: The people of Mecca ask you - O Muhammad - about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): Is he an Imam? "Say: Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true."

key_terms.إمام: Imam - divinely appointed leader and guide of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.يستنبئونك: They ask/inquire of you - the Quran's word for questioning the Prophet about a matter of truth

ai.seo_question: How does Quran 10:53 relate to the Imamate of Ali ibn Abi Talib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS), through a chain reaching Imam al-Sadiq (AS), interprets Quran 10:53 as the people of Mecca questioning Prophet Muhammad about the Imamate of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS). The answer "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true" affirms Ali's divinely appointed leadership. This hadith was narrated in the context of Shia exegetical tradition establishing Quranic proof-texts (dalil) for the Imamate, a central doctrine in Shia theology.
